practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (e.g. MONGODB_URI or DOCUMENTDB_URI) and do not commit secrets to source control.
practices.prior_belief: Never hard-code the DOCUMENTDB connection string or credentials: read the MongoDB URI from an environment variable (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and do not commit secrets to the repo.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string environment variable

practices.practice: Require TLS for client connections (include tls=true in the URI) and use SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication for Azure DocumentDB connections.
practices.prior_belief: Always enable TLS/SSL for the MongoDB connection string and verify the server certificate; ensure the connection URI uses mongodb+srv or mongodb+ssl as appropriate so traffic to the managed cluster is encrypted in transit.

practices.practice: Create a single shared MongoClient / Mongoose connection (singleton) and reuse it across the process rather than creating a new connection per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a connection pool (Mongoose/MongoClient default pooling) and reuse a single shared connection across the app instead of opening a new connection per request; set reasonable poolSize/maxPoolSize and serverSelectionTimeoutMS.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool and timeout settings for your deployment (serverless vs long-running) — e.g., small pools and low minPoolSize for serverless, larger maxPoolSize and longer maxIdleTime for OLTP servers; set serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS appropriately.

When using multi-document transactions, start a session, pass the session into every read and write that belongs to the transaction, and commit or abort explicitly (or use withTransaction when available).
practices.prior_belief: When using multi-document transactions, start a session, pass the session into all reads and writes within the transaction, and commit/abort the transaction; do not rely on implicit transactions across collections without an explicit session.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Use a TTL index (expireAfterSeconds) on an expiration Date field (e.g., expiresAt) for ephemeral entitlement/trial documents so the database automatically removes expired documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) on ephemeral entitlement/trial documents and set the TTL field as a date (e.g. expiresAt) so the database will automatically remove expired documents without application cleanup jobs.
practices.source_name: MongoDB Query Language (MQL) compatibility in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TTL index expireAfterSeconds TTL indexes expiresAt

practices.practice: Persist an idempotency marker using a unique index (for example on idempotencyKey) so duplicate attempts produce a duplicate-key error that the application can detect and handle instead of double-processing.
practices.prior_belief: Design idempotency using a unique index on an idempotency key field (e.g. idempotencyKey) and perform an insert/check inside the same transaction or use upsert semantics with handling for duplicate key errors to avoid double-billing.

practices.practice: Create indexes to match your query patterns (equality → sort → range ordering) and verify index usage with explain('executionStats') to avoid collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create appropriate indexes for query patterns used by the app (e.g. customerId on chargeEvents, subscriptionId on entitlements, unique index on idempotencyKey) and verify index usage with explain() to avoid collection scans.

practices.practice: Keep transactional scope minimal — only touch the documents that must be updated atomically to reduce conflicts and latency.
practices.prior_belief: Keep transactional scope small and limited to the minimal set of documents that must be updated atomically (e.g. insert chargeEvent + update subscription status), to reduce transaction conflicts and latency.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB documents are limited to 16 MB and transactions have a maximum lifetime (transaction timeout documented in service limits); design transactions and document sizes accordingly.
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB service limits and quotas reference
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB transaction lifetime 30 seconds document size 16 MB

practices.practice: When using Mongoose transactions, explicitly pass the session returned by startSession() into Model.create(), updateOne(), findOneAndUpdate(), etc., so those operations participate in the transaction.
practices.prior_belief: When using Mongoose, explicitly pass the session returned by startSession() into all Model.create(), Model.updateOne(), findOneAndUpdate(), etc., so the operations participate in the transaction.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB transactions pass session

practices.practice: Implement bounded retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and ensure retries are safe (idempotent) or protected by the idempotency key rather than blindly reissuing non-idempotent writes.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry logic for transient network and write errors (with exponential backoff) and be sure to make retries idempotent or protected by the idempotency key to avoid duplicate charges.

practices.practice: Disable automatic index creation in Mongoose in production (autoIndex: false) and create your indexes as part of a deployment/migration step rather than at runtime.
practices.prior_belief: Provision collections and indexes programmatically as part of deployment (scripts or migrations) and verify index creation and query plans against the live cluster rather than relying on implicit index creation at runtime.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB manage index creation deployment createIndexes vs autoIndex

practices.practice: For vector search, set retryWrites=false in the connection and create the appropriate vector index (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with correct metric and dimension settings before storing embeddings.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Vector index with Python in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index retryWrites=false vector index type HNSW DiskANN IVF

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and collect slow-query logs and metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, connections) into Log Analytics and alert on saturation or elevated retry/failed-transaction rates.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor operation metrics, slow queries and index usage (server logs, explain() output and the provider's monitoring tools) and alert on failed transactions, high retry rates, or elevated latency for critical charge flows.

practices.practice: Use least-privilege credentials for the app: create a database user limited to the application database and grant only the minimal roles/permissions required rather than using an admin/root account; consider Microsoft Entra ID and role-based access control for production.
practices.prior_belief: Limit privileges of the database user used by the application to the specific database (sample_fintech_16) and minimum required roles; do not run the app with an admin/root user credential.
practices.source_name: Migrate from Amazon DocumentDB to Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
